items.W5: Tool use and agent loops in the product

intro: Putting AI to work: directing coding agents, and building AI into the product.

concepts.name: The agent loop and the harness
concepts.what: A model in a loop with tools: it gathers context, acts, and checks. The model writes; the harness carries out the actions.
concepts.chapter: Ch 1: What Makes an Agent an Agent

concepts.name: Command line and packages
concepts.what: Running commands, files and folders, package managers.
concepts.practice: A committed change to package.json or a lockfile that adds or removes a package the product uses.

concepts.name: Launching and surfaces
concepts.what: Starting the agent in the right folder; the same engine in the terminal, desktop, IDE and web; following a session from the Claude mobile app (Remote Control); speaking prompts (/voice); non-interactive runs.
concepts.used: sessions started in the course repo; /remote-control or /voice used in sessions
concepts.made: a script that runs the agent without a person (non-interactive)
concepts.practice: /remote-control, /voice or a non-interactive run listed in the session scan's "Builder tools you used" list in the review report, or a committed script that runs the agent without a person.
concepts.chapter: Ch 1: One engine, many surfaces; Ch 2: Your phone and your voice

concepts.name: Project instructions (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md)
concepts.what: A file the agent reads at the start of every session: decisions, constraints, traps. Advisory, not enforced.
concepts.made: wrote its content (beyond the template), committed
concepts.practice: Text the student wrote in CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md beyond the template's text, committed.
concepts.chapter: Ch 2: It Knows Only What It Can See; Project Overview

concepts.name: Memory and context
concepts.what: What persists between sessions (auto memory, CLAUDE.md) and what does not; /clear and /compact.
concepts.used: memory written or /clear, /compact used in sessions
concepts.made: wrote a memory entry or rule on purpose, committed
concepts.practice: /clear, /compact or /memory listed in the session scan's "Builder tools you used" list in the review report, or a memory entry or rule the student added to CLAUDE.md or a memory file, committed.

concepts.name: Plan mode
concepts.what: Claude reads, explores and writes a plan without editing your files until you approve it. Writing the spec it builds from is Design's spec-driven development (DE20).
concepts.practice: Plan mode listed in the session scan's "Builder tools you used" list in the review report.

concepts.name: Settings and their scope
concepts.what: Project settings versus global settings, and which wins.
concepts.practice: A .claude/settings.json the student added or changed beyond the template's copy, committed.

concepts.name: Slash commands
concepts.what: Commands run by name inside a session; text after the command is its argument. Must know by name: /context, /compact, /clear, /rewind, /resume, /rename, /list-agents (/peers), /btw, /exit, /remote-control (/rc), /voice, /init, /memory, /config, /model, /effort, /status, /usage, /add-dir, /plan, /permissions, /hooks, /sandbox, /skills, /mcp, /plugin, /diff, /help.
concepts.used: slash commands used in sessions (the scan lists them)
concepts.made: wrote a custom command or skill run by name
concepts.practice: A built-in slash command listed in the session scan's "Builder tools you used" list in the review report (the course's own skills, such as /sprint-plan, /sprint-review and /learn, do not count), or a custom command the student wrote, committed.

concepts.name: Skills
concepts.what: A saved procedure the agent runs by name, shared in the repo or kept personal.
concepts.shipped: others use it (a classmate, a team, users)
concepts.practice: A skill the student wrote in .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md, committed, or a skill that is not one of the course's skills listed in the session scan's "Builder tools you used" list in the review report.

concepts.name: Hooks
concepts.what: A command that runs every time an event happens: guaranteed, unlike an instruction.
concepts.practice: A hook the student added to .claude/settings.json, committed, or a hook run listed in the session scan's "Builder tools you used" list in the review report.

concepts.name: Advice versus enforcement
concepts.what: Instructions advise; hooks and permission rules enforce. Knowing which to use for a rule.

concepts.name: Subagents
concepts.what: A separate agent with its own context, used to protect the main one or to work in parallel.
concepts.practice: Subagents listed in the session scan's "Builder tools you used" list in the review report, or a subagent file the student wrote in .claude/agents/, committed.

concepts.name: Reaching outside the repo: CLI tools, MCP servers, API calls
concepts.what: Three routes to a system outside the repo: a CLI tool the agent runs (gh, supabase), an MCP server that adds the system's actions as tools (in the Claude app, a connector), or a direct API call the agent writes with a key. Choosing the route for a case.
concepts.used: any of the three in sessions (the scan lists each)
concepts.made: added an MCP server to .mcp.json, or wrote a script or skill that wraps a CLI tool or an API
concepts.practice: A CLI tool, MCP server or API call listed in the session scan's "Builder tools you used" list in the review report, or an MCP server the student added to .mcp.json, or a committed script or skill the student wrote that wraps a CLI tool or an API.
concepts.chapter: Ch 2: Reach Beyond the Repo: CLI Tools, MCP, and APIs

concepts.name: Plugins
concepts.what: A package of skills, slash commands, subagents, hooks and MCP servers installed together with /plugin. A way to share building blocks, not a route to outside data; an enabled plugin costs context every session.
concepts.used: a plugin installed and used (its skills appear as plugin:skill)
concepts.practice: A plugin listed in the session scan's "Builder tools you used" list in the review report (its skills appear as plugin:skill), or a plugin the student wrote (.claude-plugin/plugin.json), committed.
concepts.chapter: Ch 2: Plugins: a package, not a route

concepts.name: Parallel sessions, worktrees and messaging
concepts.what: Several agents at once, each in its own working copy, and messages between them: /list-agents shows who Claude can reach; a message is plain text with no authority (it cannot approve a prompt or change settings).
concepts.used: worktrees or messages to another session in sessions (the scan counts both)
concepts.practice: Worktrees or messages to another session listed in the session scan's "Builder tools you used" list in the review report.
concepts.chapter: Ch 2: Parallel work needs separate copies of the files; Messaging your other sessions

concepts.name: Permission modes
concepts.what: Manual, Accept edits, Plan, Auto (a second model reviews each action), Don't ask (pre-approved tools only, for scripts), and Bypass permissions (--dangerously-skip-permissions: no prompts and no safety checks, for containers only). What each lets run without asking, and when to use it.
concepts.used: the modes used in sessions (the scan counts turns in each)
concepts.practice: Accept edits, Auto or Don't ask mode listed in the session scan's "Builder tools you used" list in the review report.
concepts.chapter: Ch 2: The controls, from tightest to loosest

concepts.name: Permission rules
concepts.what: Allow, ask and deny rules in a settings file: ask and deny hold in every mode, including auto and bypass; a boundary said only in chat does not.
concepts.used: a rule prompted or blocked in sessions
concepts.made: committed allow, ask or deny rules
concepts.practice: Allow, ask or deny rules the student added to a committed settings file, or a rule that prompted or blocked an action listed in the session scan's "Builder tools you used" list in the review report.
concepts.chapter: Ch 2: Rules; The controls, from tightest to loosest

concepts.name: Blast radius and undo
concepts.what: What an action can damage and what can be undone (/rewind, git); some actions are permanent.
concepts.practice: /rewind listed in the session scan's "Builder tools you used" list in the review report, or a revert commit the student made.

concepts.name: Verifying agent work
concepts.what: Done means you saw it work; a fresh-context review of agent-written code.
concepts.made: a recorded check of agent work (a review note, a test run, a check on the live site)
concepts.practice: A committed record that the student checked agent-written work (a review note, saved test output, or a note of a check on the live site) that names what was checked and the result.
concepts.chapter: Ch 2: Done Means You Saw It Work

concepts.name: Prompts as product code
concepts.what: Prompts in the product are versioned, tested and changed with reasons; examples for boundary cases.
concepts.made: a prompt file in the repo that the product uses
concepts.shipped: real users use the feature; versions kept with reasons
concepts.practice: A prompt, in a prompt file or in the code, that the product sends to a model, added or changed by the student and committed.

concepts.name: Structured output
concepts.what: Asking the model for output in a fixed shape the code can rely on.
concepts.made: a schema the product enforces on model output
concepts.practice: Committed code that asks a model for output in a fixed shape (a JSON schema, a tool definition, or a structured output setting) and parses it before the product uses it.

concepts.name: Streaming and the AI surface
concepts.what: Showing output as it arrives, and the states an AI feature passes through.
concepts.made: a streamed response in the product
concepts.practice: Committed code that shows a model's response on screen as it arrives, or a Loom moment that shows a streamed response in the product.

concepts.name: Untrusted model input
concepts.what: Text the model reads can carry instructions (prompt injection); privileged actions need a guard.
concepts.made: a guard on privileged actions in the product
concepts.shipped: real users use the guarded feature
concepts.practice: Committed code that guards an action the product takes from model output (a confirmation step, an allow list, or a check before the action runs), with a comment or record that names prompt injection or untrusted input as the reason.

concepts.name: Non-determinism
concepts.what: The same input can give different output; a feature must work across runs.

concepts.name: Tool calling and agent loops in the product
concepts.what: The model chooses the next step or calls a tool; stopping rules and a point where a person decides.
concepts.made: a loop or tool call in the product, with a stopping rule
concepts.shipped: real users rely on it; limits written down
concepts.practice: Committed code in which the model chooses the next step or calls a tool the product defines, with a stopping rule (a step limit or an end condition) in the code.

concepts.name: Evals
concepts.what: A set of cases with known answers, a baseline, noise, and graders (code for exact answers, a model as judge).
concepts.made: an eval set or scorer in the repo
concepts.shipped: a product decision made from saved results
concepts.practice: A committed set of test cases with known answers, or a scorer, for model or product output, with saved results from a run.
concepts.chapter: Ch 11: Evals: Knowing Whether It Works

concepts.name: Choosing a model by measurement
concepts.what: Picking a model by running the same cases on each, not by reputation.
concepts.made: a recorded comparison of models on the product's own cases
concepts.shipped: the product runs the chosen model for real users
concepts.practice: A committed comparison that runs the same cases on two or more models and saves the results for each.
